# Microsoft Project

Desktop scheduling tool; the primary artefact format of [[computer-project-management]] and the only
piece of proprietary tooling in the source set. Four `.mpp` files carry the entire deliverable — one
throwaway practice plan plus `export-import-system.mpp` at three maturity stages, each in its own
lab folder under the same filename.

## What the tool supplies to the coursework

Every concept the labs teach is a Project feature exercised in order:

| Feature | Recorded as |
|---|---|
| outline / indent hierarchy | [[work-breakdown-structure]] |
| FS / SS / FF task links | [[work-breakdown-structure]], [[sequence-integration-after-unit-testing]] |
| resource pool + assignment + over-allocation flags | [[resource-leveling]] |
| Save Baseline, then actuals against it | [[schedule-baseline-and-variance]] |
| the critical-path flag and tracking Gantt | [[critical-path-method]] |
| cost rollup from hourly rates | [[schedule-baseline-and-variance]] |

The critical path is a striking case: it is never computed in the repo, only *read off* a red bar
in the tracking Gantt. The tool is the algorithm.

## The format is the problem

`.mpp` is a closed binary. The repo handles that in two ways, both deliberate:

> "# Treat the binary coursework artifacts as binary — no line-ending"
> — Computer Project Management/.gitattributes, 2026-07-10

Four glob rules — `*.mpp`, `*.pptx`, `*.pdf`, `*.png` — stop git normalising or attempting to
diff/merge them. And the README supplies an escape hatch for readers without a licence: ProjectLibre
or GanttProject to open the files, or the PDF reports, which "render the full plan — schedule,
Gantt, resources and costs — with no software needed".

That escape hatch is the same instinct as [[offline-first-static-deliverable]] pointed at a
different constraint: not "no network" but "no licence". It only half works — the PDFs are the
lab 5–6 and 7–8 reports, so the earlier stages remain openable only in a scheduling tool.

**Consequence for this wiki:** the `.mpp` and `.pdf` files are unread by policy, so every
quantitative claim on the Computer Project Management pages rests on hand-written README tables
alone. That is the single largest verification gap in this group of repos and is why those pages
carry `confidence: medium`.

## Version control fit

588 KB of binaries committed raw — **no Git LFS**, despite the format being exactly the case LFS
exists for. Every edit to a plan stores a whole new copy. At four files and one publishing session
this costs nothing; on a live plan revised weekly it would. Same posture as
[[optimization-methods]], which commits an 11 MB PDF without LFS.
